title: From the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Salary to Australia’s Minimum Wage: How Hourly Pay Becomes Annual
description: Compare the Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders salary to Australia’s National Minimum Wage. Learn how to convert hourly rates to annual, fortnightly, and after-tax pay with Fair Work rule
salarySummary: At the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week, annual gross pay is approximately $52,269 before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full‑time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269. This formula gives a gross annual figure before tax and super. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for any rate.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% on top of the base hourly rate, compensating for not receiving paid leave. The National Minimum Wage for casuals is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 + 25%). If you are a casual employee, your annual estimate should use the loaded rate. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains when it applies.

faqs.q: How much superannuation do I get on top of my pay?
faqs.a: Employers must pay super guarantee of 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. For a full‑time worker on the minimum wage, that adds about $6,272 per year (12% of $52,269), up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra contribution. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for details.

bodyMarkdown:
## From Hourly to Annual: The Simple Formula

Converting an hourly rate to an annual salary is straightforward: multiply your hourly pay by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full‑time role in Australia, we assume 38 hours per week (the ordinary hours under the National Employment Standards). So the formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This gives you a gross annual figure before tax, super, and any deductions. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. If you work part‑time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

## Why the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Salary Matters

It might seem odd to compare Australian pay with American cheerleaders, but the report on the **Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders salary** highlights how vulnerable workers can be without strong minimum wage laws. In 2019, a cheerleader sued the franchise, claiming they were paid as little as $7 per hour – far below the U.S. federal minimum wage and a fraction of what Australian workers receive. Even after a reported 400% raise, the cheerleaders still lack health insurance and many work multiple jobs.

In Australia, the National Minimum Wage (from 1 July 2026) is $26.44 per hour for employees 21 and over, or $33.05 per hour for casuals (including 25% loading). That means a full‑time worker on the minimum wage earns at least $52,269 per year before tax. The contrast with the **Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders salary** shows the value of award coverage and the Fair Work system.

## National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor, but most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher rates. Awards specify minimum pay for different classifications, plus penalties, allowances, and overtime. For example, a retail employee might earn $27–$30 per hour depending on their level. Always check your award using the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) or the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate because they don’t get paid sick leave or annual leave. The casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour. When using our calculator, you can tick the “casual” checkbox to add the loading automatically. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the tool handles it for you.

## Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a full‑time worker on the minimum wage:

- Weekly: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80

This is before tax and super. Use our [timesheet](/) to track your hours and see your pay per period.

## Tax and Medicare

Tax is withheld from your pay by your employer using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 + 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 + 37% of excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: $51,370 + 45% of excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). For a minimum‑wage earner on $52,269, the estimated tax is about $4,020 + 30% of ($52,269 – $45,000) = $6,201, plus Medicare of $1,045, giving a take‑home of around $45,023 per year. See [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) for a detailed breakdown.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top of your salary. It does not reduce your take‑home pay. For a $52,269 salary, super adds $6,272 per year (up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base). This is separate from your wages and goes into a super fund. Learn more on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Using the Calculator

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and choose whether you are casual. It calculates annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, plus estimated tax and super. Remember: the results are estimates. For exact pay, refer to your award or agreement.

### Key Assumptions

- 38‑hour week for full‑time
- No unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances
- No salary sacrifice
- Super at 12% of ordinary earnings, capped at $270,830
- 2026–27 tax rates with full tax‑free threshold
- Medicare levy based on 2025–26 single thresholds

## Conclusion

Whether you’re comparing the **Dallas Cowboys cheerleaders salary** or your own hourly rate, understanding the conversion to annual pay helps you budget and negotiate. Australia’s minimum wage and award system provide a strong safety net, but always check your specific entitlements. Use our [reference tables](/data) for award rates and the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page to see how your earnings compare nationally.
